findings.summary: When exactly one of --phase-one-receipt and --producer-keyring is supplied, the pair-incomplete violation is recorded but neither supplied reference is resolved or shape-checked. Thus an independently checkable bad supplied path/JSON/keyring is still hidden until a later run, contradicting the stated per-input pre-flight aggregation guarantee.

A phase-one receipt is only checked to be a JSON object before cross-route validation is skipped for a malformed keyring. A malformed route object plus malformed keyring consequently reports only the keyring violation, although the phase-one form is independently checkable.

The PUB1 regression intentionally supplies three independently malformed pre-flight inputs: an escaping report, a malformed phase-one receipt (`{"kind":"not-a-route"}`), and a malformed keyring. It then asserts exactly two violations and only checks report/keyring messages. This contradicts the frozen D2 guarantee that every route reference is independently resolved and shape-checked; a checker that silently omits malformed phase-one receipt validation will pass this regression.

When exactly one of --phase-one-receipt and --producer-keyring is supplied, the pair-incomplete violation is recorded but neither supplied reference is resolved or shape-checked. This omits an independently checkable pre-flight violation contrary to the declared D2 guarantee.

A malformed phase-one receipt route form is not reported when the keyring is malformed, although receipt form validation is independently checkable. The checker consequently aggregates only the keyring violation.

The PUB1 regression supplies malformed report, phase-one receipt, and keyring inputs but asserts only two violations and does not require the receipt-form violation, allowing the incomplete aggregation behavior to pass.
